page.layout: One block of text, one printed page on the scan. Running head "PRÆFATIO." above the text at top centre. No marginal notes beyond a short catchword-like word "Mens" set between two lines of verse, treated as part of the text.

main_text.p: Ἡ̔ovτα (ut de Themistocle Thucydides pronunciauit) turpe enim est reperacta demum intelligere quid fieri debuisset.

Si qui formæ elegantia præcellunt, dent operam, ut virtutum & εὐλογοφαθίας decus illam perinde illustret, quemadmodum lumen quod in oculis est, Solis radijs illustratur, ut vsui sit homini. Est enim formæ nitor & elegantia, bonum alienum, ut Bioni Borysthenitı: donū natura, ut Aristoteli: exigui temporis tyrannis mox deflorescens, ut Socrati: naturæ prærogatiua quæ paucis contingit, ut Platoni: fraus silens & absque verbis persuadens, ut Theophrasto: eburneum detrimentum, ut Theocrito: regnum ἀδ̔ορυφόρητον, absque satellitio, ut Carneadi, visum est. Et verè dicitur:
main_text.l: Forma, color, uires pereunt: ceu lilia: sed
main_text.p: Si qui facultatibus opum instructi sunt, meminerint illas instrumenta & administicula virtutis esse. Ideò enim & Paulus Apostolus ait: Iis qui divites sunt in hoc seculo,

page.notes: Left-hand edge of page and the faint show-through of the reverse side are not transcribed. Several words are damaged where the paper is stained and the ink is faint, notably "instructi", "instrumenta" and "divites"; these are given as best read. The Greek words in the first and third paragraphs are copied from the scan but may be imperfectly reproduced. The line "Mens" is printed in a smaller, separate position between two lines of verse. The verse line "Luce Dei fulgens, prima manet." is partly obscured and should be checked against the original. The last line "culo," is printed at the far right and is the end of the page's text.
